unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The vehicle must be a qualifying new or used battery-electric or hydrogen model from a participating seller, within the published price and model-year limits.
name: MyFirstEV
short_description: A point-of-sale incentive for a first zero-emission vehicle, offered while participating automakers have funding.
description: MyFirstEV reduces the purchase or lease price of a first-time buyer’s qualifying new or used battery-electric or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle. Participating automakers apply the incentive at sale. Plug-in hybrids are not eligible. New vehicles generally must be model year 2026 or newer with an MSRP of $50,000 or less, except for California-headquartered ZEV-only manufacturers. Used vehicles generally must be manufacturer certified pre-owned, at least two model years older, and $25,000 or less, with the same manufacturer exemption. Vehicles ordered before a manufacturer offers the incentive are not eligible. Availability varies by automaker and dealership and lasts only while funds remain. Dealer/channel and model-list requirements are not evaluated by this site.
benefit_summary: Up to $3,500 off a new ZEV or $1,750 off a used ZEV at participating sellers

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be below 300% of the federal poverty level, and the replacement vehicle must meet the program’s published vehicle rules.
name: Driving Clean Assistance Program
short_description: Statewide scrap-and-replace vehicle assistance for income-eligible households outside participating air-district Clean Cars 4 All programs.
description: DCAP’s Clean Cars 4 All scrap-and-replace pathway is open. The financing-assistance (no-scrap) pathway is closed because funding was depleted. Applicants must be approved before buying or leasing. Replacement vehicle price generally cannot exceed $45,000 before tax and fees. Income must be below 300% of the federal poverty level using the program’s published household-size chart; this site does not convert that chart into a single income number. Residents of air districts that run their own Clean Cars 4 All programs must use those district programs instead. Official DCAP and MyFirstEV pages currently disagree about stacking with other CARB programs.
benefit_summary: Up to $12,000 toward a replacement clean vehicle, plus charging help on some awards

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be at or below 300% of the federal poverty level, and you must live in the Bay Area air district’s service area.
name: Bay Area Clean Cars for All
administrator: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
short_description: Bay Area scrap-and-replace incentive for income-eligible residents in the air district’s jurisdiction.
description: The Bay Area air district’s Clean Cars for All program is open. Income must be at or below 300% of the federal poverty level. Applications on or after July 1, 2026 use total income, not AGI. Residents must live in the district’s jurisdiction. This site does not evaluate ZIP lists or FPL tables, so income and exact service-area details stay unresolved.
benefit_summary: Income-eligible scrap-and-replace incentive in the Bay Area air district

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must live in the San Diego County air district and meet the program’s published scrap-and-replace rules.
name: San Diego Clean Cars 4 All
administrator: San Diego County Air Pollution Control District
short_description: San Diego County scrap-and-replace incentive for qualifying low-income residents.
description: The San Diego County APCD passenger-vehicle page states that the San Diego region Clean Cars 4 All program is open. The consumer site is sdcc4a.org. The district HTML page does not publish a current dollar table, so amounts are left blank. Incentives are not retroactive. County residence is required.
benefit_summary: Incentive funding for qualifying low-income San Diego County residents

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The vehicle must meet Smog Check and ownership rules. Higher awards also require an income test that is not fully checked here.
name: BAR Consumer Assistance Program Vehicle Retirement
short_description: Cash to retire an eligible vehicle at a BAR-contracted dismantler after you receive a letter of eligibility.
description: BAR pays $1,350 without an income test if the vehicle failed its most recent Smog Check, or $1,500 / $2,000 for income-eligible households depending on pass/fail status. Income-qualified awards use 225% of the federal poverty level; BAR publishes a calculator rather than a dollar table on the retirement page. Do not retire the vehicle before the letter of eligibility. Funds depend on each fiscal year.
benefit_summary: $1,350 to $2,000 to retire an eligible vehicle

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be at or below 225% of the federal poverty level, and repairs must follow BAR’s published station and approval rules.
name: BAR Consumer Assistance Program Repair Assistance
short_description: Help paying for emissions repairs after a failed biennial Smog Check, after you receive a letter of eligibility.
description: Income-eligible owners (225% of the federal poverty level) may receive up to $1,450 for 1996 and newer vehicles or up to $1,100 for 1976–1995 vehicles. A consumer copay applies. Do not start CAP repairs before the letter of eligibility. Work must be done at a STAR test-and-repair station.
benefit_summary: Up to $1,450 toward qualifying emissions repairs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The vehicle, purchase timing, and income-qualified path must meet PG&E’s published pre-owned EV rebate rules.
name: PG&E Pre-Owned EV Rebate
short_description: Rebate for a used electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle on an active PG&E electric residential account.
description: Standard rebate is $1,000. Rebate Plus is $4,000 for income-qualified customers. Apply after purchase, generally within 90 days. Standard applications must be complete by September 30, 2026; from October 1, 2026 only the income-qualified path continues. The same vehicle cannot also receive the SCE or SDG&E pre-owned EV rebate or a Clean Fuel Reward on that VIN.
benefit_summary: $1,000 standard or $4,000 income-qualified used-EV rebate

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The vehicle, purchase timing, and income-qualified path must meet SCE’s published pre-owned EV rebate rules.
name: SCE Pre-Owned EV Rebate
short_description: Rebate for a used EV or PHEV for SCE residential customers.
description: Standard rebate is $1,000. Plus is $4,000 for income-qualified customers. Apply within 180 days of purchase. Optional pre-approval can reserve funds. Cannot stack on the same vehicle with PG&E or SDG&E pre-owned EV rebates or a Clean Fuel Reward.
benefit_summary: $1,000 standard or $4,000 income-qualified used-EV rebate

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The vehicle, purchase timing, household limits, and income-qualified path must meet SDG&E’s published pre-owned EV rebate rules.
name: SDG&E Pre-Owned EV Rebate
short_description: Rebate for a used EV or PHEV for SDG&E residential customers.
description: Standard rebate is $1,000. Plus is $4,000 for income-qualified customers. Apply within 180 days. One rebate per person and one application per household for the program lifetime. Cannot stack on the same vehicle with PG&E or SCE pre-owned EV rebates or a Clean Fuel Reward.
benefit_summary: $1,000 standard or $4,000 income-qualified used-EV rebate

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The used EV must be on LADWP’s approved list and meet the age, registration, VIN, and prior-rebate rules, and your permanent residence must receive LADWP electricity.
name: LADWP Used Electric Vehicle Rebate Program
administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
short_description: Rebate for a qualifying used EV or plug-in hybrid at a permanent residence served by LADWP electricity.
description: The standard rebate is $1,500. Households whose LADWP service address is on EZ-SAVE or Lifeline at purchase and through rebate issuance can receive up to $4,000. Purchase before approval is allowed; apply after purchase, generally within 12 months. You do not have to be the LADWP account holder, but the permanent residence must receive LADWP electric service. The vehicle must be on LADWP’s approved used-EV list, at least two model years older than the application calendar year and not older than eight years, registered to the applicant at the service address, and within LADWP’s VIN/prior-rebate limits (including the 24-month wait after a prior rebate on the same VIN). Confirm eligibility before buying. Terms reviewed on the official page remain current as of September 7, 2026.
benefit_summary: $1,500 standard, or up to $4,000 on EZ-SAVE or Lifeline

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a PG&E customer installing listed charging equipment under the published rebate path.
name: PG&E Residential EV Charging Rebate
short_description: Rebate for a listed home EV charger, with a higher income-qualified path.
description: Standard path reimburses up to 50% of the purchase price of listed equipment after installation. Rebate Plus can cover up to $2,000 for charger installation or up to $5,000 for a panel plus charger. One rebate per household service agreement. Standard applications are post-install within 180 days of equipment purchase.
benefit_summary: Up to 50% of charger cost, or up to $5,000 on the income-qualified path

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be an SCE customer, and income or disadvantaged-community rules may apply for the published rebate amount.
name: SCE Charge Ready Home
short_description: Rebate to upgrade a home electrical panel for EV charging.
description: Charge Ready Home describes rebates of up to $4,200 for income-qualified customers or up to $2,100 in disadvantaged communities for a home electrical-panel upgrade. A licensed contractor is required. SCE marketing copy about a $4,200 Level 2 charger rebate within 120 days of getting an EV is not treated as a separate amount here.
benefit_summary: Up to $4,200 toward a qualifying home electrical-panel upgrade

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be the LADWP residential electric account holder installing a listed qualifying charger under the published equipment and installation rules.
name: LADWP Residential EV Charger Rebate
administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
short_description: Rebate for a home EV charger and installation on an LADWP residential account.
description: LADWP residential electric account holders may receive up to $1,000 toward a qualifying Level 2 home charger and installation. Senior/Disability Lifeline or EZ-SAVE participants may receive an additional $500 (up to $1,500). An optional $250 dedicated EV meter rebate can be selected on the same application. The applicant must be the name on an active LADWP residential electric account. Qualifying charger models, electrical-service assessment, and installation details are not evaluated here. LADWP recommends a service assessment before installation.
benefit_summary: Up to $1,000, or up to $1,500 on Lifeline or EZ-SAVE, plus an optional $250 meter rebate

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a SMUD customer, and Energy Assistance Program Rate status may change what is covered.
name: SMUD Charge@Home
short_description: Rebate or free charger installation for SMUD customers charging at home.
description: Charge@Home can reimburse up to $600 for equipment and/or circuit work. Energy Assistance Program Rate customers may receive a free Level 2 charger and qualifying circuit work; panel upgrades are not covered. Apply through SMUD’s Charge at Home pages.
benefit_summary: Up to $600, or a free charger path for EAPR customers

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have a valid California driver license, meet the income rules, and have a good driving record.
name: California Low Cost Automobile Insurance
short_description: State-sponsored liability insurance for income-eligible good drivers who need to meet California’s insurance law.
description: CLCA offers income-eligible California residents liability coverage that meets the state’s financial-responsibility law. Official pages require a valid California driver license, a vehicle valued at $25,000 or less, income eligibility, and a good driving record. Premiums vary by county. This is insurance, not a rebate. Apply at mylowcostauto.com or through a certified agent.
benefit_summary: Income-eligible liability insurance at program rates

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must live in Los Angeles County and meet the published household-income table or be enrolled in a listed public-benefit program.
name: LA Metro LIFE Program
administrator: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
short_description: Free and discounted transit rides for qualifying Los Angeles County residents.
description: LIFE is for Los Angeles County residents who meet a published household-income table or who are enrolled in a listed public benefit such as CalFresh, Medi-Cal, reduced-price school meals, SNAP, Social Security, SSDI, or TANF. After approval, riders receive unlimited free rides for 90 days on participating systems, then 20 free regional rides each month. A household-size income table is published on Metro’s official page and is not converted into a single engine limit here. Temporary South LA and Pomona extra-month promotions are not treated as the standing countywide benefit. Apply through Metro’s LIFE page.
benefit_summary: Unlimited free rides for 90 days after approval, then 20 free regional rides each month

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must live in the South Coast AQMD jurisdiction and meet the published older-vehicle and household-income rules.
name: South Coast AQMD Replace Your Ride
administrator: South Coast Air Quality Management District
short_description: Up to $12,000 to replace a qualifying older vehicle, or choose an e-bike or transit-card alternative.
description: Qualified applicants who live in the South Coast AQMD jurisdiction and meet the program’s income and older-vehicle rules can receive up to $12,000 to replace that vehicle with a newer cleaner vehicle, including a plug-in hybrid, battery-electric, or fuel-cell vehicle. Instead of a replacement car, an applicant may choose an e-bike or an alternative public-transportation charge card. This site cannot evaluate air-district boundaries, so jurisdiction stays an unmodeled required condition and is not stored as county or ZIP geography. Apply through the official Replace Your Ride site.
benefit_summary: Up to $12,000 toward a qualifying replacement vehicle, e-bike, or transit alternative

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, or you must qualify through a listed assistance program.
name: California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE)
short_description: A monthly discount on electricity and/or natural gas for income-qualified customers of participating investor-owned utilities.
description: CARE typically discounts electricity about 30–35% at large electric utilities and natural gas about 20%, plus a reduced base service charge on some tariffs. Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level using the CPUC table effective June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027, or through listed public-assistance programs. This site does not convert that household-size table into one income number. Apply with your utility. LADWP and SMUD use separate municipal discounts, not CARE.
benefit_summary: About 20–35% off qualifying utility charges

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Household size must be at least three, and income must fall between the CARE limit and 250% of the federal poverty level.
name: Family Electric Rate Assistance (FERA)
short_description: An 18% electricity discount for households that earn too much for CARE but still meet FERA’s income band.
description: FERA is electricity-only and cannot be combined with CARE. It is offered by PG&E, SCE, and SDG&E. Income must fall between the CARE ceiling and 250% of the federal poverty level on the June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027 table. This site does not hard-code that table as a single income limit.
benefit_summary: About 18% off electricity, plus a reduced base charge on some tariffs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, or you must qualify through a listed assistance program.
name: Energy Savings Assistance
short_description: No-cost energy-efficiency and weatherization upgrades for income-qualified IOU customers.
description: ESA can install insulation, efficient appliances, weatherstripping, and other measures at no charge if you qualify. Income must be at or below 250% of the federal poverty level on the June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027 table, or through listed assistance programs. Renters and owners may qualify; landlord permission can be required. Apply with PG&E, SCE, SDG&E, or SoCalGas. This is the statewide CPUC program, not a separate record per utility.
benefit_summary: No-cost home energy upgrades if you qualify

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: A licensed medical practitioner must certify a qualifying medical condition or life-support equipment.
name: Medical Baseline Allowance
short_description: Extra energy at the lowest baseline rate for households that need electricity or gas for a qualifying medical condition.
description: Medical Baseline is not income-based. A licensed medical practitioner must certify a qualifying condition or life-support equipment. Extra kilowatt-hours or therms are billed at the lowest baseline rate. Recertification is typically required. Apply with your IOU. LADWP and SMUD have separate medical/life-support discounts.
benefit_summary: Additional baseline-rate energy for qualifying medical needs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet the published state-median-income table, and help depends on local funding.
name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
administrator: California Department of Community Services and Development
short_description: Once-a-year help paying an energy bill, plus crisis help and some weatherization, through local CSD providers.
description: LIHEAP can make a once-a-year bill payment (HEAP), provide emergency crisis help (ECIP), and offer weatherization. There is no statewide published dollar benefit. Income uses CSD’s 2026 monthly table based on 60% of state median income; this site does not encode that table as one number. Apply through a local service provider, not a single statewide form. Funds are limited.
benefit_summary: Once-a-year energy bill help and crisis assistance if funds remain

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet the published weatherization table, and a local provider must be able to serve your home.
name: Weatherization Assistance Program
administrator: California Department of Community Services and Development
short_description: Free weatherization and related health-and-safety work for income-eligible homeowners and renters.
description: DOE Weatherization Assistance in California is administered by CSD and local providers. Measures can include sealing, insulation, HVAC, and water heaters after an energy audit. Income uses the CSD table effective July 1, 2026. No statewide dollar cap is published. Owners and renters may qualify.
benefit_summary: No-cost weatherization if a local provider can serve your home

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be CARE or FERA eligible and live in a designated disadvantaged community, and enrollment capacity may be limited.
name: Disadvantaged Communities Green Tariff
short_description: 20% off the electric rate plus 100% renewable supply for CARE/FERA-eligible customers in designated disadvantaged communities, when capacity exists.
description: DAC-GT, often branded Green Saver, is usually automatic if you are CARE or FERA eligible and live in a qualifying disadvantaged community. Capacity is limited; PG&E reports it is at capacity and enrolls when space opens. This site cannot evaluate CalEnviroScreen geography, so location remains unresolved beyond utility service.
benefit_summary: 20% off the electric rate plus 100% renewable supply, if capacity is available

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must already be on CARE or FERA and meet the published past-due balance and payment rules.
name: Arrearage Management Plan
short_description: Forgives a share of past-due IOU bills after 12 on-time current-bill payments, for CARE or FERA customers.
description: AMP can forgive 1/12 of eligible arrears after each on-time payment of the current bill, up to $8,000 after 12 on-time payments. You must already be on CARE or FERA and meet past-due thresholds. CPUC records schedule the pilot to sunset October 1, 2026; IOU pages still described enrollment as of September 6, 2026.
benefit_summary: Up to $8,000 of eligible arrears forgiven after 12 on-time payments

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet LADWP’s published EZ-SAVE table for your household size.
name: LADWP EZ-SAVE
administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
short_description: Income-qualified discount on LADWP bills. Lifeline is a separate larger discount for seniors or people with disabilities.
description: EZ-SAVE is LADWP’s municipal bill-discount program, not CPUC CARE. The official page describes savings but does not publish a percent. The income table on the page was labeled effective July 1, 2025 and had not been replaced by a 2026–27 table at verification. Apply through an LADWP account.
benefit_summary: Income-qualified discount on LADWP electric and water bills

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet SMUD’s published federal-poverty-level bands for the Energy Assistance Program Rate.
name: SMUD Energy Assistance Program Rate
short_description: A monthly electric-bill discount for income-qualified SMUD customers.
description: EAPR monthly discounts are published by federal-poverty band: up to $105 (0–50% FPL, including a rate-stabilization amount), $42 (50–100%), $20 (100–150%), or $10 (150–200%). Income table effective February 1, 2026. This is SMUD’s municipal rate, not CARE.
benefit_summary: Monthly discount of $10 to $105 depending on income band

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must enroll a listed connected thermostat and meet Power Savers participation rules.
name: LADWP Power Savers
administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
short_description: Prepaid-card incentives for LADWP customers who enroll a qualifying connected thermostat in demand response.
description: Power Savers pays a $55 prepaid card after acceptance, then an annual participation incentive of $40 for 25%–75% event participation or $90 for more than 75% participation. The published household maximum is currently $145. You need an eligible connected or smart thermostat configured to central air conditioning and must agree to remote adjustments during the season. Qualifying thermostat models and event-participation rules are not evaluated here. Geography is LADWP electric service.
benefit_summary: $55 after acceptance, plus $40 or $90 for participation, currently up to $145 per household

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have a qualifying disconnection notice, meet the 200% federal poverty level income test, and not have received REACH this calendar year.
name: PG&E REACH
short_description: A one-time PG&E bill credit of up to $800 for income-eligible customers with a disconnection notice.
description: Relief for Energy Assistance through Community Help (REACH) applies an energy credit of up to $800 toward the past-due portion of a PG&E bill. Official 2026 eligibility includes a 15-day or 48-hour disconnection notice, no REACH award in the same calendar year, and income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level using CARE guidelines. AMP customers are not eligible. Funding is first-come. The income table is not encoded as a single household_income number.
benefit_summary: Up to $800 toward a past-due PG&E bill

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be below 400% of the federal poverty level, and the past-due balance and payment rules must be met.
name: PG&E Match My Payment
short_description: Dollar-for-dollar matching of qualifying payments toward a past-due PG&E bill, up to $1,000.
description: PG&E’s official Match My Payment page offers a match of every dollar you pay, up to $1,000, toward a past-due balance of at least $100. You must make a $50–$1,000 payment after enrollment. Income must be below 400% of the federal poverty level through May 31, 2027. AMP customers are not eligible. Funding is first-come. The 400% FPL table is not encoded as a single household_income number.
benefit_summary: Up to $1,000 in matching payments toward a past-due PG&E bill

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet the published CARE table, and assistance is limited to once in a 12-month period.
name: SCE Energy Assistance Fund
short_description: One-time SCE bill help of up to $200, or $300 for an all-electric household.
description: SCE’s Energy Assistance Fund, administered with United Way, can apply up to $200 (or $300 for an all-electric household) toward an SCE bill once in a 12-month period. Official income guidelines on the page match the June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027 CARE table. Those household-size amounts are not encoded as a single income number.
benefit_summary: Up to $200, or $300 for an all-electric household, toward an SCE bill

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have a final disconnection notice, an open account at your primary residence, and no Neighbor-to-Neighbor pledge in the past 12 months.
name: SDG&E Neighbor-to-Neighbor
short_description: Up to $300 toward past-due SDG&E charges for customers with a final disconnection notice.
description: SDG&E’s official Neighbor-to-Neighbor page offers up to $300 toward past-due balances for residential customers who have a final notice before disconnection, have an open account at their primary residence, and have not received an NTN pledge in the past 12 months. The program is shareholder-funded. Hardship reasons are case-specific and are not encoded.
benefit_summary: Up to $300 toward a past-due SDG&E bill

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have qualifying earned income and meet the published CalEITC filing and qualifying-child rules.
name: California Earned Income Tax Credit
short_description: A refundable California tax credit for working people and families with earned income up to the published annual cap.
description: For tax year 2025, FTB published a maximum CalEITC of $3,756 and a maximum earned-income limit of $32,900. Amounts depend on qualifying children. Claim it on a California return with FTB 3514. Tax year 2026 tables were not posted at verification. This site does not treat the $32,900 figure as a current-year engine rule.
benefit_summary: Up to $3,756 for tax year 2025, depending on earned income and qualifying children

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: A qualifying child must be under 6, and you generally must also qualify for CalEITC.
name: Young Child Tax Credit
short_description: A refundable California credit for families with a qualifying child under 6 who generally also qualify for CalEITC.
description: For tax year 2025, FTB published a maximum Young Child Tax Credit of $1,189 per eligible return. You generally must qualify for CalEITC and have a child under 6. A zero-income exception exists. Claim it with FTB 3514.
benefit_summary: Up to $1,189 per eligible tax return for tax year 2025

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be 18–25 at year-end, qualify for CalEITC, and have qualifying California foster-care history.
name: Foster Youth Tax Credit
short_description: A refundable credit for eligible former California foster youth who qualify for CalEITC.
description: For tax year 2025, FTB published up to $1,189 per eligible individual, or $2,378 if both spouses or RDPs qualify. You must qualify for CalEITC, be 18–25 at year-end, and have been in California foster care at age 13 or older. CDSS verification is required.
benefit_summary: Up to $1,189 per eligible person for tax year 2025

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income limits depend on filing status, you must have paid rent for at least half the year, and you cannot have claimed a homeowners’ exemption.
name: California Nonrefundable Renter’s Credit
short_description: A nonrefundable credit if you paid rent in California for at least half the year and meet the income limits.
description: FTB’s page last updated February 20, 2026 lists a $60 or $120 credit and California income limits of $53,994 (single or separate) or $107,987 (joint, head of household, or qualifying widow). You must have paid rent for at least half the year and not have received a homeowners’ exemption. The credit is claimed on the California return.
benefit_summary: $60 or $120 nonrefundable credit, depending on filing status

name: Homeowners’ Property Tax Exemption
short_description: A $7,000 reduction in taxable value for an owner-occupied principal residence.
description: The California Constitution provides a $7,000 reduction in taxable value for a qualifying owner-occupied home on the January 1 lien date. BOE says this generally equals about $70 at the 1% statewide rate, more if local bonds exceed 1%. File BOE-266 with the county assessor. This is not a cash payment.
benefit_summary: $7,000 reduction in assessed value (about $70 at the 1% rate)

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income, resources, and household composition must meet CalFresh rules, including the net-income test.
name: CalFresh
short_description: Monthly EBT food benefits for income-eligible individuals and families.
description: CalFresh is California’s SNAP program. CDSS published 2025–2026 income and allotment tables effective October 1, 2025–September 30, 2026. Maximum monthly allotments range from $298 (1 person) to $1,789 (8 people). Apply through BenefitsCal or a county office. This site does not encode the full SNAP net-income test.
benefit_summary: Monthly food benefits; up to $994 for a household of four on the 2025–26 table

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be ineligible for CalFresh solely because of immigration-status rules and still meet CalFresh income tests.
name: California Food Assistance Program
short_description: State-funded food benefits for some noncitizens who are ineligible for federal CalFresh solely because of immigration status.
description: CFAP uses the same application path as CalFresh. It currently covers people ineligible for CalFresh solely due to PRWORA immigration rules. The expansion to all income-eligible people age 55 and older regardless of immigration status is not implemented and is anticipated October 1, 2027. No separate dollar table is published.
benefit_summary: State-funded food benefits through the CalFresh application

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The child must be eligible through CalFresh, CalWORKs, school meals, or an approved summer application.
name: SUN Bucks (Summer EBT)
short_description: A $120 summer food benefit for each eligible child.
description: SUN Bucks provides $120 per eligible child for the summer. Many children on CalFresh, CalWORKs, or free/reduced-price meals are enrolled automatically. Others apply through a school meal application or UBA. The deadline to apply for summer 2026 was August 31, 2026; later applications are for 2027. The program itself remains a current annual benefit.
benefit_summary: $120 per eligible child each summer

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a current or former CalWORKs recipient in an approved activity, and the child must meet the age rules.
name: CalWORKs Child Care
short_description: Help paying for child care for current or former CalWORKs recipients who are working or in approved activities.
description: Stages 1–3 help current or former CalWORKs families pay a provider of their choice. Care is generally for children through age 12 (or up to 21 with qualifying disabilities). There is no published consumer cash amount. Apply through the county welfare department. This is not CalWORKs cash aid itself.
benefit_summary: Voucher payments to a child-care provider you choose

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must be at or below 85% of state median income, and a local agency must have an available voucher.
name: California Alternative Payment Program
short_description: Child-care vouchers for eligible low-income families, paid directly to the provider.
description: CAPP uses federal and state funding for vouchers at licensed or license-exempt care. Local Alternative Payment agencies administer enrollment and often have waitlists. CDSS does not publish a consumer dollar benefit. Income uses an 85% state-median-income ceiling that this site does not convert into one number.
benefit_summary: A voucher that pays an eligible child-care provider

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet the published state-median-income preschool ceilings, and a local contractor must have space.
name: California State Preschool Program
short_description: Part-day or full-day preschool for income-eligible families and other qualifying categories.
description: CSPP income eligibility is at or below 100% of state median income, with limited enrollment up to 115%. CDE published FY 2026–27 ceilings effective July 1, 2026. Apply through a local contractor. This site does not encode the full SMI table.
benefit_summary: No-cost or subsidized preschool if a local contractor has space

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The child must be in an eligible foster or emergency placement in a participating county.
name: Emergency Child Care Bridge Program for Foster Children
short_description: A time-limited child-care voucher and navigator help for foster and emergency placements. Not an entitlement.
description: The Bridge Program is a time-limited bridge to longer-term child care. Counties opt in. Initial vouchers are generally 6 months and may be extended. Apply through county child welfare or a local resource and referral agency.
benefit_summary: Time-limited child-care voucher for eligible foster placements

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income or participation in a qualifying assistance program must meet California LifeLine rules.
name: California LifeLine
short_description: A monthly discount on home phone or cell service for income-qualified or program-qualified households.
description: California LifeLine can discount service up to $19 per month, or up to $28.25 when combined with federal Lifeline. Connection discounts of up to $39 are also published. Income limits effective June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027 start at $24,600 for a one-person household. One discount per household except TTY/DDTP. Start with a participating provider.
benefit_summary: Up to $19 per month, or up to $28.25 with federal Lifeline

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must meet California LifeLine eligibility for this broadband discount.
name: California LifeLine Home Broadband Pilot
short_description: A three-year pilot that adds a broadband discount for California LifeLine-eligible households.
description: Decision 25-08-050 launched a technology-neutral broadband pilot on January 26, 2026. Official amounts are up to $20 per month for standalone fixed broadband or $30 for a broadband-and-voice bundle, plus a connection reimbursement of up to $39 once per year. Eligibility follows California LifeLine rules.
benefit_summary: Up to $20 or $30 per month toward home broadband

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be pregnant, a new parent, or caring for a child under 5, and income must meet the published WIC tables.
name: California WIC
short_description: Nutrition food benefits, education, and breastfeeding support for pregnant people, new parents, and young children.
description: California WIC provides healthy foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals. It serves infants and children up to age 5 and people who are pregnant or recently gave birth. Official pages confirmed on September 6, 2026 that WIC offices remain open and continue to enroll families. Income limits follow federal WIC tables and are not encoded as a single household_income number.
benefit_summary: Monthly food benefits plus nutrition support

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income, resources, and family composition must meet CalWORKs rules.
name: CalWORKs
short_description: Cash aid and employment services for eligible families with children.
description: CalWORKs is California’s TANF program. County welfare departments determine eligibility from income, resources, and family composition. Families apply through BenefitsCal or a county office. Income and household-composition tests are not encoded as a single household_income rule.
benefit_summary: Monthly cash aid and employment services

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet Medi-Cal’s federal-poverty-level rules, and citizenship or immigration rules may apply.
name: Medi-Cal
administrator: California Department of Health Care Services
short_description: California’s Medicaid program covering medical, dental, mental health, and long-term care.
description: Medi-Cal is California’s Medicaid program. Covered California’s official Medi-Cal page describes income tests that use federal poverty level percentages (for example 138% FPL for many adults). Those percentage tables are not encoded as a raw household_income number. Apply through Covered California, BenefitsCal, or a county office.
benefit_summary: No- or low-cost health coverage

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Premium help depends on household income, household size, and location, which are not fully calculated here.
name: Covered California
short_description: State health insurance marketplace with premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions.
description: Covered California is the official ACA marketplace. Financial help depends on household income, household size, and location. Those subsidy calculations are not encoded as a single household_income cutoff.
benefit_summary: Premium tax credits and reduced-cost health plans

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be eligible for Medi-Cal and need in-home care because of age, blindness, or disability.
name: In-Home Supportive Services
short_description: Paid in-home care for eligible older adults and people with disabilities.
description: IHSS pays for personal care and household services so eligible aged, blind, or disabled people can remain at home. Official eligibility includes California residency, a Medi-Cal determination, and living in one’s own home. County social workers determine hours. Age and disability are not reduced to a single required profile field because younger disabled applicants can qualify.
benefit_summary: Paid in-home care hours

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be aged, blind, or disabled, ineligible for SSI/SSP solely due to immigration status, and meet resource rules.
name: Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants
short_description: State cash aid for certain aged, blind, or disabled immigrants who are ineligible for SSI/SSP solely due to immigration status.
description: CAPI provides monthly cash benefits equivalent to SSI/SSP payment standards for eligible non-citizens who cannot receive SSI/SSP solely because of immigration status. Apply with a county social services agency using SOC 814. Immigration, disability, and resource tests are not encoded in the current profile.
benefit_summary: Monthly cash assistance equivalent to SSI/SSP standards

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The student must attend a participating California public or charter school that serves the meals.
name: California Universal Meals
short_description: Free school breakfast and lunch for students at participating California public schools.
description: California’s Universal Meals Program requires participating public school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools serving TK–12 to provide a nutritionally adequate breakfast and lunch free of charge each school day to students who request a meal, regardless of household income. Households do not file a separate statewide application for the meals themselves.
benefit_summary: Free school breakfast and lunch at participating public schools

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must file a timely FAFSA or CADAA, have a verified GPA, and meet Cal Grant income, asset, and school rules.
name: Cal Grant
short_description: State grants for eligible California college students that do not need to be repaid.
description: Cal Grants help pay tuition and education costs at qualifying California colleges. Students are considered after a timely FAFSA or CADAA and a verified GPA. Income, asset, and school-eligibility tests are determined by CSAC and are not reduced to a single household_income rule.
benefit_summary: College grant aid that does not need to be repaid

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must attend an eligible UC, CSU, or CCC bachelor’s program and meet CSAC income and asset rules.
name: Middle Class Scholarship
short_description: CSAC scholarship for eligible UC, CSU, and CCC bachelor’s-degree students.
description: The Middle Class Scholarship reduces remaining college costs after other aid. CSAC published an income/asset ceiling of up to $250,000 for students attending July 2026–June 2027. Award amounts depend on CSAC calculations and available funding, so that ceiling is not encoded as a single engine cutoff.
benefit_summary: College cost-of-attendance scholarship

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: SSA must determine that you qualify for SSI using federal income and resource rules.
name: State Supplementary Payment
short_description: California’s state supplement to federal SSI for eligible aged, blind, or disabled people.
description: SSP is paid with federal SSI. SSA determines SSI/SSP eligibility using federal criteria. This catalog does not encode SSA income or resource tests. People ineligible for SSI/SSP solely due to immigration status may instead look at CAPI.
benefit_summary: Monthly state cash supplement to SSI

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The child must have been born in California on or after July 1, 2022, or otherwise qualify as a listed public-school student.
name: CalKIDS
administrator: ScholarShare Investment Board / California Student Aid Commission
short_description: State-funded college scholarship accounts for eligible California children and students.
description: CalKIDS provides scholarship accounts that families claim. Official pages state that children born in California on or after July 1, 2022 have an account, and certain public-school students also qualify. Award amounts vary by birth year and student status. This is not a household income-matching program and has no encoded income rule.
benefit_summary: Claimable college scholarship account

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You generally must have earned at least $300 and paid into State Disability Insurance, and the leave reason must qualify.
name: California Paid Family Leave
short_description: Short-term wage replacement for bonding with a new child, caring for a seriously ill family member, or military-family assist.
description: EDD’s Paid Family Leave program pays 8 weeks of benefits in a 12-month period if you qualify. Official weekly amounts published on September 6, 2026 range from $50 to $1,765. You generally must have earned at least $300 and paid into SDI. Job protection comes from other laws, not PFL itself.
benefit_summary: Up to 8 weeks of wage replacement, $50 to $1,765 per week

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You generally must have earned at least $300 with SDI withheld, and a qualifying non-work-related disability must keep you from working.
name: California State Disability Insurance
short_description: Short-term wage replacement when you cannot work because of a non-work-related disability.
description: EDD Disability Insurance pays people who lose wages because of a non-work-related illness, injury, pregnancy, childbirth, surgery, or qualifying rehabilitation. Official weekly amounts published on September 6, 2026 range from $50 to $1,765 for up to 52 weeks. You generally must have earned at least $300 with SDI withheld.
benefit_summary: Wage replacement of $50 to $1,765 per week for up to 52 weeks

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: County income limits, first-time buyer rules, and an eligible first mortgage must be met. This is repayable financing.
name: CalHFA MyHome Assistance Program
short_description: A deferred junior loan for down payment and closing costs through a CalHFA-approved lender.
description: MyHome is a deferred-payment junior loan. With an FHA first mortgage it can be the lesser of 3.5% of purchase price or appraised value; with a conventional first it can be the lesser of 3%. CalHFA is not a direct lender. County income limits apply and are not encoded here as a single number. This is repayable financing, not free savings.
benefit_summary: Deferred junior loan of about 3% to 3.5% of the purchase

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Loan, occupancy, and lender rules must be met. This is repayable financing.
name: GSFA Platinum Down Payment Assistance
short_description: A second-mortgage down-payment product through GSFA participating lenders. First-time buyer status is not required.
description: Platinum Standard can provide up to 5% of the first-mortgage amount as a 15-year amortizing second. Select can combine a 3.5% second with a gift of up to 1.5% subject to market conditions. Maximum first mortgage published is $832,750. This is repayable financing.
benefit_summary: Second-mortgage assistance up to 5% of the first mortgage

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be employed by a listed GSFA member county, and the home must be a primary residence.
name: GSFA Assist-to-Own
short_description: Deferred 0% second-mortgage help for people employed by a GSFA member county.
description: Assist-to-Own can provide a deferred 0% second of 3.5% of the first-mortgage amount and a gift of up to 2% subject to market conditions. Employment with a listed GSFA member county must be verified. The home can be anywhere in California as a primary residence. This is not a general public DPA.
benefit_summary: Deferred 0% second of 3.5%, plus a possible gift up to 2%

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home must be in a listed disaster area with qualifying damage, and income generally must be at or below 120% of area median income.
name: ReCoverCA Homeowner Rehabilitation
administrator: California Department of Housing and Community Development
short_description: Help for eligible homeowners to repair or rebuild homes damaged in the 2023 and 2024 severe storms.
description: HCD’s page stated the application period is open and funding is limited. Eligible 2023 storm areas include Monterey, San Benito, Santa Cruz, Tulare, Tuolumne, and the Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation; 2024 storms include San Diego County. Damage generally must be at least $8,000. Income generally must be at or below 120% AMI. This is disaster rehabilitation, not a market-rate loan shopper product.
benefit_summary: Repair or rebuild assistance for eligible disaster-damaged homes

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home must be in an eligible rural area, and income must be very low on USDA county tables.
name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair Loans and Grants
short_description: Very-low-income rural homeowners can get a 1% repair loan and, if age 62 or older, a grant.
description: California is in a pilot that publishes grants up to $10,000, loans up to $40,000, and combined assistance up to $50,000. The home must be in an eligible rural area. Income must be very low by USDA county tables. Grants generally must be repaid if the home is sold within three years. This is rural housing assistance, not a city rebate.
benefit_summary: Loans up to $40,000 and grants up to $10,000 (combined up to $50,000 in the CA pilot)

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income must meet the published low-income limits, and after-rehab value cannot exceed the posted cap.
name: Fresno County Owner-Occupied Rehabilitation Program
short_description: 0% loans for eligible Fresno County homeowners to fix health-and-safety problems.
description: OORP provides loans to federally eligible low-income owner-occupants. After-rehab value cannot exceed $396,000 (effective September 1, 2025). Contact the Community Development Division; there is no self-serve portal.
benefit_summary: 0% rehabilitation loan for eligible owner-occupants

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must meet the first-time buyer definition and the published income limits.
name: Kings County First-Time Homebuyer Program
short_description: Deferred gap financing for qualified first-time buyers in unincorporated Kings County.
description: The official CDBG page describes a deferred second-position loan for the life of the first loan or until sale. No single dollar cap is published on that page. Apply through Self-Help Enterprises or the County CDA.
benefit_summary: Deferred second-position gap financing

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income and property rules must meet the county rehabilitation guidelines.
name: Kings County Housing Rehabilitation Program
short_description: Rehabilitation assistance for eligible Kings County homeowners.
description: The official CDBG page lists a Housing Rehabilitation Program and points applicants to Self-Help Enterprises and the County CDA. A single dollar cap is not published on that page.
benefit_summary: Home rehabilitation loan for eligible owners

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Priority census-tract and occupancy rules apply, and funding is limited.
name: Los Angeles County Greenline Home Program
administrator: Los Angeles County Department of Consumer and Business Affairs
short_description: A $35,000 down-payment or closing-cost grant for eligible first-time buyers in Los Angeles County.
description: The official page describes a $35,000 grant with a three-year occupancy lien and urges applicants to contact Neighborhood Housing Services before funds are exhausted. Priority is given to high-need census tracts. This is county consumer assistance, not a separate CalHome record.
benefit_summary: $35,000 down-payment or closing-cost grant

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home must be in the listed unincorporated supervisorial districts, occupied at least one year, and income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income.
name: LACDA Handyworker Program
short_description: Grants up to $9,000 for eligible owner-occupants in specified unincorporated districts.
description: The property must be in unincorporated areas of Supervisorial Districts 1, 4, or 5. Owners must have occupied the home at least one year. Income generally must be at or below 80% AMI. This site cannot evaluate supervisorial-district maps, so geography stays at county level and is conservative.
benefit_summary: Grant up to $9,000 for qualifying repairs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home must be in a listed unincorporated district, occupied at least 12 months, and income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income.
name: LACDA Senior Grant Program
short_description: Grants up to $20,000 for mobility and functionality repairs for seniors 62 and older.
description: Eligible homeowners in specified unincorporated districts who are 62 or older and at or below 80% AMI may receive up to $20,000. Occupancy of at least 12 months is required.
benefit_summary: Grant up to $20,000 for qualifying senior home repairs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a first-time buyer with no ownership in the last three years, use a participating lender, and buy in an eligible area.
name: LACDA Home Ownership Program
short_description: A 0% deferred loan of up to $100,000 or 20% of the price, through a HOP lender only.
description: Only a HOP participating lender can submit an application. Assistance is the lesser of $100,000 or 20% of purchase price. First-time buyers (no ownership in the last three years) must owner-occupy a home in unincorporated Los Angeles County or a participating city. This is repayable deferred financing.
benefit_summary: Deferred loan up to $100,000 or 20% of the purchase price

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income, and only a participating lender can submit an application.
name: Los Angeles Low Income Purchase Assistance
short_description: A deferred shared-appreciation loan of up to $161,000 for first-time buyers in the City of Los Angeles.
description: LIPA reservations are limited. The official page (modified August 18, 2026) listed later 2026 reservation windows and a maximum purchase price of $956,465. Income generally must be at or below 80% AMI. Apply only through an LAHD participating lender.
benefit_summary: Deferred loan up to $161,000

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income and reservation-window rules apply, and only a participating lender can submit an application.
name: Los Angeles Moderate Income Purchase Assistance
short_description: Subordinate purchase assistance for moderate-income first-time buyers in the City of Los Angeles.
description: MIPA uses the same participating-lender reservation process as LIPA. The official page listed September and December 2026 reservation windows with limited slots. A dollar maximum was not restated on the MIPA page at verification.
benefit_summary: Subordinate loan for moderate-income first-time buyers

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home must be a qualifying City of Los Angeles single-family house or most mobile homes, income limits apply, and you must be 62 or older and/or have a permanent disability. Funding and waitlists can change.
name: LAHD Handyworker
short_description: Up to $5,000 in no-cost modifications or repairs for qualifying City of Los Angeles homeowners.
description: The City of Los Angeles Handyworker program can provide up to $5,000 in no-cost modifications and repairs for a qualifying single-family home or most mobile homes inside the city. Income limits apply. The homeowner generally must be age 62 or older and/or have a permanent disability; those age-or-disability and income tests are not encoded as a single pass/fail rule. Demand may create a waiting list, and help depends on available funding. This is the city LAHD program, not the separate LACDA county Handyworker grant.
benefit_summary: Up to $5,000 in no-cost modifications or repairs

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income, and city funding must still be available.
name: City of Monterey Emergency Repair Loan
short_description: Deferred 5% emergency repair loans for owner-occupants in the City of Monterey.
description: The city accepts applications subject to posted deadlines and funding. Loans are deferred 5% simple interest and due on sale, title change, or 30 years. Income generally must be at or below 80% AMI. A separate major-rehab loan of up to $90,000 is described on the same page and is not imported as a second program.
benefit_summary: Deferred emergency repair loan

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: The home generally must be within 20 miles of the workplace, and income must meet county guidelines.
name: Napa County Proximity Housing Homebuyer Assistance
short_description: Down-payment assistance up to 16.5% for people who work in Napa County.
description: The county is accepting online applications through its Neighborly portal. The home generally must be within 20 miles of the workplace. Income limits are published in county guidelines and are not encoded here as a single number.
benefit_summary: Down-payment assistance up to 16.5% of the purchase

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income.
name: City of Napa Housing Rehabilitation
short_description: 0% loans up to $75,000 and emergency grants up to $5,000 for eligible City of Napa owners.
description: The city’s 2026 materials describe 0% loans of up to $75,000 due in 20 years and emergency grants of up to $5,000. Income generally must be at or below 80% AMI.
benefit_summary: 0% loans up to $75,000 and emergency grants up to $5,000

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income, occupancy, and remaining-funds rules must be confirmed with the county before a purchase contract.
name: Nevada County Down Payment Assistance
short_description: A $50,000 deferred down-payment loan for eligible Nevada County buyers.
description: The official page publishes a $50,000 deferred 3% simple-interest loan due in 30 years or on sale. Contact the county before entering a purchase contract to confirm funds remain.
benefit_summary: $50,000 deferred down-payment loan

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Local employment and a deed restriction apply.
name: Placer County Workforce Housing Preservation Program
short_description: Down-payment help of up to 16% of the purchase price in exchange for a workforce deed restriction in eastern Placer County.
description: The official page says the program continues to accept applications and that the assistance does not need to be paid back if program rules are met. Local employment and a deed restriction apply. This is not the closed Placer first-time-homebuyer loan window.
benefit_summary: Up to 16% of the purchase price toward a down payment

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a full-time permanent County or HACSM employee for at least 18 months and cannot already own in San Mateo County.
name: San Mateo County Employee Down Payment Assistance
administrator: County of San Mateo Department of Housing
short_description: A $100,000 second mortgage for eligible County or housing-authority employees, awarded by quarterly lottery.
description: Applicants must be full-time permanent County or HACSM employees for at least 18 months and cannot already own in San Mateo County. The next drawing published at verification was September 22, 2026. This is an employee program, not general public DPA.
benefit_summary: $100,000 second mortgage, plus a possible $5,000 moving grant

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income and property rules must meet the Housing Authority guidelines.
name: Stanislaus County Housing Rehabilitation Program
administrator: Stanislaus County / Housing Authority of the County of Stanislaus
short_description: Grants and low-interest loans for income-eligible homeowners to fix health-and-safety problems.
description: The official county page still directs applicants to the Housing Authority. A single dollar cap is not published on the landing page.
benefit_summary: Health-and-safety rehabilitation grants or loans

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must meet the first-time buyer definition and the published income limits.
name: Tuolumne County First-Time Homebuyer Program
short_description: Income-qualified first-time buyer assistance administered by the county housing division.
description: The official FAQ states the program is available for income-qualified households. A dollar cap is not published on that FAQ.
benefit_summary: Income-qualified first-time buyer assistance

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income and owner-occupancy rules must meet the county rehabilitation guidelines.
name: Tuolumne County Owner-Occupied Rehabilitation
short_description: Rehabilitation assistance for income-qualified owner-occupants.
description: The official FAQ states the Housing Division manages an owner-occupied rehabilitation program for income-qualified households. A current dollar cap is not published on that FAQ.
benefit_summary: Owner-occupied rehabilitation assistance

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have at least 40% equity and household income at or below the published limit, among other Controller requirements.
name: California Property Tax Postponement
short_description: A repayable deferral of current-year property taxes for eligible senior, blind, or disabled homeowners.
description: The State Controller’s Property Tax Postponement Program lets qualifying homeowners defer current-year property taxes on a principal residence. Official 2026–27 criteria include at least 40% equity and household income of $57,002 or less, among other requirements. The deferral is secured by a lien and must eventually be repaid. This is financing, not free savings. The 2026–27 filing period opens October 1, 2026 and closes February 10, 2027. Applications became available in September 2026. Income, equity, and disability/age tests are not encoded as a single pass/fail rule.
benefit_summary: Repayable deferral of current-year property taxes if you qualify

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: Income generally must be at or below 80% of area median income or meet categorical eligibility, and the home must be in a designated community focus area.
name: Equitable Building Decarbonization Statewide Direct Install
short_description: No-cost electric appliances and efficiency upgrades for eligible low-income homes in designated under-resourced communities.
description: EBD Statewide Direct Install provides and installs upgrades at no cost. Eligibility generally includes income at or below 80% AMI or categorical eligibility, plus residence in a designated community focus area. Renters need an owner participation agreement. This site cannot evaluate unofficial ZIP lists, so geography stays unresolved beyond statewide California.
benefit_summary: No-cost electric appliances and related upgrades if your community is in a current focus area

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must meet CARE or FERA guidelines and live in a top 25% CalEnviroScreen disadvantaged community or California Indian Country.
name: DAC-SASH
short_description: No-cost or low-cost rooftop solar for income-qualified homeowners in disadvantaged communities or California Indian Country.
description: GRID Alternatives administers DAC-SASH for PG&E, SCE, and SDG&E customers who meet CARE/FERA guidelines and live in a top 25% CalEnviroScreen disadvantaged community or California Indian Country. The handbook incentive is $3/W CEC-AC. This site cannot evaluate CalEnviroScreen tracts.
benefit_summary: No-cost or low-cost rooftop solar if GRID determines you qualify

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a SoCalGas customer installing a listed qualifying product while funds remain.
name: SoCalGas Home Energy Efficiency Rebates
short_description: 2026 rebates for qualifying gas appliances and solar thermal equipment.
description: SoCalGas publishes 2026 rebate amounts including dryers, tankless and storage water heaters, furnaces, fireplace inserts, pool heaters, ovens, patio heaters, and solar thermal. Funds are first-come, first-served through December 31, 2026 or until exhausted.
benefit_summary: Device rebates from $70 up to $5,000 depending on equipment

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be an LADWP residential electric customer installing a listed qualifying product that meets that measure’s published technical and documentation rules.
name: LADWP Consumer Rebate Program
administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
short_description: One LADWP umbrella rebate for listed residential efficiency measures, not a separate program per product.
description: The Consumer Rebate Program is a single residential rebate path for listed measures. Standing published amounts include heat-pump HVAC up to $2,500 per ton, ENERGY STAR heat-pump water heaters up to $2,500 per unit, ENERGY STAR windows $2 per square foot, cool roofs up to $0.60 per square foot, whole-house fans $200, and variable-speed or variable-flow pool pumps $500. Conventional HVAC rebates of $100–$120 per ton are also listed. A summer 2026 promotion pays $750 for a qualifying pool pump purchased and installed between June 1 and September 30, 2026, with applications due by December 31, 2026; that higher amount is temporary and is not the standing maximum. You must be an LADWP residential customer with active electric service. Purchase and install before applying; applications generally must be postmarked within 12 months of purchase. Per-measure permit, rating, and documentation rules are not encoded here.
benefit_summary: Standing rebates up to $2,500 per heat-pump water heater or per ton of heat-pump HVAC

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a SMUD customer, and a participating contractor must submit the rebate.
name: SMUD Home Performance and Go Electric Rebates
short_description: Contractor-submitted rebates for heat-pump water heaters, HVAC packages, and related electrification.
description: SMUD publishes heat-pump water heater rebates of $3,000–$4,000 for gas-to-electric replacements depending on tank size, a Go Electric bonus of up to $2,000, and HVAC packages of up to $3,000. Rebates are subject to funding and must be submitted by a participating contractor.
benefit_summary: Heat-pump water heater rebates of $3,000 to $4,000, plus other package rebates

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a Clean Power Alliance CARE or FERA customer.
name: Clean Power Alliance Instant AC Savings
short_description: A $300 instant coupon for a room air conditioner for CARE or FERA customers.
description: CPA’s official FAQ describes a $300 Instant AC Savings coupon for eligible CARE/FERA customers.
benefit_summary: $300 instant coupon for a qualifying room air conditioner

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a Clean Power Alliance customer, and PSPS, medical, or income adders have extra rules.
name: Clean Power Alliance Sun Storage Rebate
short_description: Battery rebate of up to $2,250 for CPA customers, first-come while funding lasts.
description: Official stack: $750 base, plus $1,250 for PSPS-affected homes, plus $250 medical or $250 income (those two adders are not combined). Maximum published is $2,250.
benefit_summary: Up to $2,250 toward an eligible home battery

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must have lived in the single-family home for at least 12 months and be an MCE customer.
name: MCE Heat Pump Rebates
short_description: Heat-pump water heater and HVAC rebates through MCE participating contractors. Not retroactive.
description: Official amounts include heat-pump water heaters up to $3,175 and heat-pump HVAC up to $400 per 500 square feet plus a $2,000 bonus. The homeowner must own a single-family detached home lived in for at least 12 months.
benefit_summary: Heat-pump water heater rebate up to $3,175, plus HVAC rebates

unmodeled_required_criteria_summary: You must be a Peninsula Clean Energy customer installing a listed upgrade.
name: Peninsula Clean Energy Home Upgrade Rebates
short_description: Appliance electrification rebates for PCE customers, including San Mateo County and Los Banos.
description: WestLight Energy / PCE rebates remain available until the program ends or funding runs out. Terms were updated May 18, 2026. Heat-pump HVAC replacing gas is published at $1,500; other tiers are on the official page. Apply after installation.
